notes: encoding::json follows Go 1.27's behaviour (v1 implemented on v2) byte for byte: Marshal/Unmarshal/Decoder/Encoder map to the Serialize/Deserialize traits (derive macros take Go struct tags), the scanner, Compact/Indent/HTMLEscape, token stream and error values (text, offsets, paths) are differential-tested against Go, and Value is the interface{} target. Rust-shaped differences: Unmarshal returns the decoded value rather than filling a pointer (unmarshal_into and Decoder::decode_into decode into an existing value with Go's merge rules), and nil versus empty slices/maps do not exist (Vec/BTreeMap are always empty, Option is nil); Value objects are insertion-ordered (struct fields in declaration order, map keys and decoded text sorted); reflect.Type fields are Go-style type name strings; Bytes is the []byte-as-base64 type; Value parses with FromStr and prints with Display.

CallMethodsWithLegacySemantics.note: Go's pointer-receiver rule depends on whether a reflected value is addressable; Rust has no such distinction (a Serialize impl is called on any value), so both settings call the same methods and the option is recorded only.

Compact.note: appends to a Vec<u8> instead of a bytes.Buffer; returns the SyntaxError, nothing is appended on error

Decoder.Buffered.note: returns the buffered bytes (a &[u8] is an io.Reader); the buffer fill pattern follows jsontext, so the bytes match Go's for any reader

Decoder.Decode.note: generic over the target type, returns the value; end of input is Error::Eof

Decoder.Token.note: returns the Token enum; Error::Eof and the unexpected-EOF io error mark the end

FormatByteArrayAsArray.note: [u8; N] cannot get an encoding different from [T; N] without specialization, so byte arrays always encode as arrays of numbers (the v1 form).

FormatBytesWithLegacySemantics.note: Implemented for the part Rust can express: with false, decoding a JSON array into Bytes is an error (differential-checked against Go's v2). Named byte types and marshal methods on bytes do not exist here, so the other effects have nothing to change.

FormatDurationAsNano.note: With false, std::time::Duration has no JSON form: marshal fails with 'unsupported value: no default representation' and unmarshal with the matching UnmarshalTypeError, as Go's v2 default does (unit-tested; the Go typed registry has no Duration field).

Indent.note: appends to a Vec<u8>; returns the SyntaxError, nothing is appended on error

InvalidUTF8Error.note: deprecated and never returned, as in Go: invalid UTF-8 is replaced with U+FFFD

InvalidUTF8Error.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

InvalidUnmarshalError.note: the type and its text exist; the typed Rust API cannot be given a nil or non-pointer destination, so unmarshal never returns it

InvalidUnmarshalError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

InvalidUnmarshalError.Type.note: reflect.Type is a Go-style type name; None is Go's nil type

MarshalerError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

MarshalerError.Type.note: reflect.Type is a Go-style type name; like Go 1.27 it is the pointer type

MatchCaseSensitiveDelimiter.note: false makes decoding ignore - and _ when matching keys to fields; checked against jsonv2 by tools/json_check.py

MergeWithLegacySemantics.note: Unmarshal returns a new value instead of filling a destination, so there is no existing value to merge into; the option is recorded only.

Number.note: Number::new and FromStr validate, so an invalid Number cannot exist: the error Go's Marshal returns for an invalid json.Number (MarshalerError for *json.Number, cannot parse as JSON number) is returned at construction; the empty text stays valid and marshals as 0

Number.MarshalJSONTo.note: the jsontext streaming hook is the Serialize impl of Number: the literal was validated at construction (Go's MarshalerError text is the Number::new error), so serializing cannot fail

Number.UnmarshalJSONFrom.note: the jsontext streaming hook is the Deserialize impl of Number: numbers and quoted numbers decode, other values give Go's position-less UnmarshalTypeError

OmitEmptyWithLegacySemantics.note: false omits fields whose encoding is null, "", [] or {}; checked against jsonv2 by tools/json_check.py

Options.note: a set of option settings with join; consumed by marshal_with_options and unmarshal_with_options

ParseBytesWithLooseRFC4648.note: With false, \r and \n in the base64 text of Bytes are errors ('illegal character ... at offset n') instead of ignored; differential-checked against Go.

ParseTimeWithLooseRFC3339.note: Not implemented. time::Time has marshal_json/unmarshal_json, but this module provides no Serialize/Deserialize for it, so the option has nothing to select between (Go's loose time.Parse versus the strict RFC 3339 grammar). Recorded only; this is the one json entry whose deviation status is a scope call rather than an impossibility.

ReportErrorsWithLegacySemantics.note: The Error enum mirrors v1's error types and texts; the v2 error shapes (SemanticError and friends) belong to encoding/json/v2 and jsontext, which are outside this crate, so false is recorded only.

StringifyWithLegacySemantics.note: false makes the string tag option quote only numbers, for encoding and decoding; checked against jsonv2 by tools/json_check.py

SyntaxError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

Token.note: an enum of Delim, Bool, Float64, Number, String and Null instead of an interface{}

Unmarshal.note: Unmarshal returns the decoded value, or only the error after a type error: Go fills the destination as far as it can and returns the UnmarshalTypeError with it. Decoding into an existing value is unmarshal_into; there is no nil versus empty.

UnmarshalArrayFromAnyLength.note: false requires JSON arrays to match the length of Rust arrays; checked against jsonv2 by tools/json_check.py

UnmarshalFieldError.note: deprecated and never returned, as in Go

UnmarshalFieldError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

UnmarshalFieldError.Type.note: reflect.Type is a Go-style type name

UnmarshalTypeError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

UnmarshalTypeError.Type.note: reflect.Type is a Go-style type name

UnsupportedTypeError.note: every Rust type with a Serialize impl is encodable, so marshal does not return it; the type and its text exist

UnsupportedTypeError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

UnsupportedTypeError.Type.note: reflect.Type is a Go-style type name

UnsupportedValueError.Error.note: the Display text is Go's Error() string

UnsupportedValueError.Value.note: reflect.Value is a description of the value
